suite.description: Byte-exact LFCP Wire interoperability vectors: Principals, Control Records, ownership transfer, Key Packages, Data Units, invitation URI, session messages and negative validation cases.
suite.warning: All private keys, DEKs and derived keys in this suite are public test fixtures. They MUST NOT be used in production or as production defaults.

cases.note: Frontier from the accepted Data Units: BOB 1..2 (D1, D2; D3 is past the C6 cutoff) and CAROL 1 (D4).
Frontier with an extra range: the BOB entry of DATA_HAVE_with_hole (1..100, 105..107) and CAROL 1. Not derived from D1-D4.

error.detail: STALE_DATA_EPOCH / quarantine because Bob cutoff at epoch 0 is seq=2

cases.description: D1 sealed under a non-deterministically encoded AAD
cases.note: Client-local rejection (SPEC-PATCH-01 / N3): only a client holding the DEK can detect it; there is no wire error code.

mutation.field: AAD encoding of the actor sequence (seq 1)

rule.text: When an LFCP algorithm requires reconstructing a deterministic structure, such as AEAD AAD, HPKE `info`, or HPKE AAD, the reconstructed structure MUST follow these deterministic CBOR rules exactly. (§26.3: a Data Unit is eligible for merge only if "the unit decrypts successfully"; "A client MUST NOT merge a Data Unit that fails AEAD authentication and SHOULD surface it to the application.")

derivation.why: The receiver reconstructs the canonical AAD, so decryption fails; accepting it would require guessing alternative encodings of signed or authenticated structures.

cases.description: D1 wrapped in COSE_Sign1 tag 18

rule.text: A strict LFCP-WIRE-01 implementation MUST reject a tagged persistent LFCP object as non-canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: The object ID is SHA-256 of the exact bytes; a tagged copy would be a second, different object for the same content.

cases.description: D1 with one signature bit flipped

rule.text: A receiver MUST reject a signed object whose signature does not verify under the public key of the Principal named by `kid` [...]. It reports `INVALID_SIGNATURE`.

derivation.why: An unverified signature lets anyone inject Data Units in the actor's name.

cases.description: D1 payload signed by CAROL (kid CAROL) instead of the actor BOB

rule.text: A receiver MUST reject a signed object [...] whose `kid` does not identify the Principal the object requires as signer (for example, the actor of a Data Unit). It reports `INVALID_SIGNATURE`.

derivation.why: The signature is valid but by the wrong Principal; accepting it lets one member forge another member's edits.

cases.description: D1 ciphertext sealed under the AAD of sequence 2
cases.note: Client-local rejection (SPEC-PATCH-01 / N3): only a client holding the DEK can detect it; there is no wire error code.

mutation.field: AAD actor sequence used for sealing

rule.text: A Data Unit is eligible for merge only if: [...] 6. the unit decrypts successfully [...] A client MUST NOT merge a Data Unit that fails AEAD authentication and SHOULD surface it to the application.

derivation.why: The AAD binds the ciphertext to its resource, epoch, actor and position; accepting it would let ciphertext be replayed elsewhere.

cases.description: CONTROL_PUT of C6 with expected head C4 while the coordinator head is C5

rule.text: If not equal, it MUST return `NACK(CONTROL_HEAD_MISMATCH)` with the current head.

derivation.why: Compare-and-swap is what keeps the Control Chain linear; committing against a stale head would fork it.

cases.description: A second Control Record at sequence 6 on top of C5

rule.text: Two different validly signed records referencing the same previous Control Record create a Control Fork. A client MUST NOT silently choose a branch. Neither record is accepted as the Control Head; a receiver that refuses a competing record reports `CONTROL_CONFLICT`.

derivation.why: Choosing a branch silently would let replicas diverge on authorization and keys.

cases.description: D1 re-issued with actor sequence 0

rule.text: Sequence numbers begin at `1`. A receiver MUST reject a Data Unit with actor sequence `0` with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Sequence 0 is outside the per-actor sequence space, so Have Vectors and hash chains cannot describe it.

cases.description: D1 with a previous-unit reference although it is sequence 1

rule.text: For sequence `1`, it MUST be `null`. [...] A gap or mismatch MUST be reported to the sync engine.

derivation.why: The actor hash chain must start at sequence 1; a non-null link there breaks gap and equivocation detection.

cases.description: KP0 payload names CAROL as recipient but is sealed to BOB
cases.note: Client-local rejection (SPEC-PATCH-01 / N5): the package is ignored and surfaced; there is no wire error code.

rule.text: The HPKE `info` value is deterministic CBOR encoding of ["LFCP-KEY-v1", resource-id, data epoch, recipient]. [...] A package that does not open for its named recipient, or whose DEK does not match the commitment, is ignored and SHOULD be surfaced to the application. This is a client-local decision [...]

derivation.why: HPKE info binds the recipient; a package that does not open for its named recipient delivers no key.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-01 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 2

rule.text: 2. key `2` MUST be omitted when there are no extra ranges; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 4

rule.text: 4. each sequence range MUST have `start <= end`; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 5

rule.text: 5. ranges MUST be strictly above `contiguous`; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 6

rule.text: 6. ranges MUST be sorted by ascending `start`, then ascending `end`; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 7

rule.text: 7. ranges MUST be non-overlapping; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 8

rule.text: 8. ranges MUST be non-adjacent; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-01 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 9

rule.text: 9. no two `actor-have` entries for the same Principal MAY occur in one canonical frontier. (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-01 with CAROL listed before BOB

rule.text: Entries MUST be sorted by ascending raw 32-byte `principal-id`, compared lexicographically as unsigned bytes. [...] A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one entry order.

cases.description: CAROL Data Unit in closed epoch 0, where C6 records no CAROL entry

rule.text: If an actor is absent from the recorded frontier, no newly discovered Data Units from that actor in the closed epoch are automatically acceptable. Any later-arriving previous-epoch unit beyond that frontier MUST NOT be merged automatically. A server that receives such a unit in `DATA_PUT` responds `NACK(STALE_DATA_EPOCH)`; a client keeps it in quarantine. [...] It SHOULD be surfaced to the application as stale offline work [...]

derivation.why: The cutoff frontier makes revocation deterministic; merging late closed-epoch work would let removed members keep writing.

cases.description: D1 payload with a non-shortest integer encoding, re-signed

mutation.field: payload encoding of the data epoch (0)

rule.text: A receiver MUST also reject a persistent signed object whose protected-header bytes or payload bytes are not the deterministic encoding of their own decoded value. [...] any difference is rejected with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Two byte forms of one payload would be two objects with different IDs for the same content.

cases.description: BOB Principal Descriptor with an additional field 3

rule.text: A Principal Descriptor with any field other than `0`, `1` and `2` is invalid; the map is closed, as the CDDL above defines it.

derivation.why: An open descriptor would let two byte forms describe one Principal and carry unauthenticated data next to its keys.

cases.description: D1 signed with a small-order R that cofactored (ZIP-215) verification accepts

rule.text: A verifier MUST reject the signature, with `INVALID_SIGNATURE`, when any of the following holds: [...] 3. `A` or `R` is a point of small order;

derivation.why: R is the neutral element and S = k·a, so both the cofactorless and the cofactored equations hold; only the small-order rule makes every implementation reject it alike.

cases.description: Principal Descriptor whose Ed25519 key is a point of small order

mutation.field: Ed25519 public key (field 1), with the ID recomputed

rule.text: A receiver MUST also validate the Ed25519 public key in field `1` whenever a descriptor is received: it MUST be a canonical point encoding and MUST NOT be a point of small order, as defined in Section 10.5.1. A descriptor whose key fails this check is invalid.

derivation.why: A small-order key admits signatures that verify for many messages; rejecting it at receipt keeps such a Principal out of every authorization decision.

error.detail: AUTH_FAILED when received in HELLO or AUTH (LFCP-WIRE-01 §7)
